raw_segments.text: A majority taken collectively may be regarded as a being whose opinions, and most frequently
whose interests, are opposed to those of another being, which is styled a minority.
If it be admitted that a man, possessing absolute power, may misuse that power by wronging his
adversaries, why should a majority not be liable to the same reproach?
Men are not apt to change their characters by agglomeration, nor does their patience
in the presence of obstacles increase with the consciousness of their strength.
See, and for these reasons, I can never willingly invest any number of my fellow creatures with
that unlimited authority, which I should refuse to any one of them.
